oidc_jwt.description: When authentication uses the SAML connector, requesting offline_access does not yield refresh token support.
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of refresh_token for SAML-backed logins is by design and should not be flagged as freshness or session-management failure.

oidc_jwt.description: Dex rotates refresh tokens on every refresh by default.
oidc_jwt.note: A previously issued refresh token becoming invalid after use is expected and should not be treated as session corruption.

oidc_jwt.description: For the OIDC upstream connector, groups claims refresh only when the ID token is refreshed; regular refresh flow does not update groups, and groups are disabled by default unless insecureEnableGroups is set.
oidc_jwt.note: Group mismatches or stale group membership across refreshes may be by design rather than authorization-binding failure.

oidc_jwt.description: When getUserInfo is enabled on the OIDC connector, UserInfo claims take priority over claims returned by the ID token.
oidc_jwt.note: Differences between upstream ID token claims and resulting Dex claims may be by design due to UserInfo precedence.

oidc_jwt.description: Public clients without explicit redirectURIs only support redirects beginning with http://localhost or the special urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob URL.
oidc_jwt.note: Redirect rejection for other URIs on public clients is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: For the OIDC connector, groups claims only refresh when the ID token is refreshed; regular refresh flow does not update groups claims.
oidc_jwt.note: Group staleness across ordinary refresh operations is documented behavior and can look like an authorization-binding bug if not accounted for.

oidc_jwt.description: Dex can intentionally issue ID tokens whose aud is a different client than the one that initiated login when the target client trusts the requester via trustedPeers.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-client audience changes are by design in trusted-peer setups and should not be flagged as audience confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Dex token exchange always returns the issued token in the access_token field, with the actual token type indicated separately by issued_token_type.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not misclassify this as field confusion; the docs explicitly call out this RFC 8693 behavior.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Dex documentation in this corpus exposes configuration primarily via static config file and gRPC API, not documented HTTP admin endpoints. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume REST setup operations such as enable_auth_method, create_policy, create_application, or cleanup_auth_method exist for Dex HTTP; only documented OIDC/OAuth endpoints should be exercised over HTTP.

For I3 flow-coherence tests on authorization code flow, the sequence MUST bind authorize and token exchange with the same redirect_uri and returned code/state. Dex documentation describes standard OAuth2 code flow and state validation; using a mismatched redirect_uri or swapped state/code tests client misuse rather than Dex behavior.

For I2 expired_token and future_token controls against Dex-issued JWTs, the fuzzer SHOULD include a control login using a valid code/token flow in the same environment. Dex docs note configurable expiry for idTokens and authRequests; without a control, token rejection may be caused by expired auth code, bad client config, or unsupported grant setup rather than JWT freshness enforcement.

For I1 request-object tests at /auth, Dex certification results explicitly include 'unsigned-request-object-supported-correctly-or-rejected-as-unsupported' as unresolved. The fuzzer MUST treat rejection and explicit unsupported behavior as acceptable outcomes; only successful processing of attacker-controlled unsigned request parameters should be considered suspicious.

For I3 config-change sequences involving token exchange, Dex token exchange works only with an OIDC connector and requires the token-exchange grant to be enabled (default) plus connector_id in the request. The fuzzer MUST configure an OIDC upstream connector and include connector_id, otherwise failures are setup errors, not security findings.

For I5 token-exchange scope escalation tests, Dex allows scopes such as openid, email, profile, groups, federated:id, and audience:server:client_id:(client-id). The fuzzer MUST compare returned claims against requested scope because Dex documentation states claims are scope-driven; requesting broader scope in the exchange can legitimately broaden returned claims if policy permits.

For I5 cross-client audience tests, Dex supports cross-client trust only when the target client explicitly lists the acting client in trustedPeers and the request uses scope audience:server:client_id:(client-id). The fuzzer MUST configure trustedPeers before expecting cross-client audience issuance; otherwise rejection is by design.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience, Dex-issued tokens are client-bound and audience-sensitive per docs. The fuzzer MUST distinguish between access_token and id_token semantics: session_token for subsequent API use is access_token, while audience examples in docs often describe id_token aud/azp. Do not flag differences caused solely by token type.

For I2 replay_same_token on JWT bearer inputs, Dex token exchange accepts externally obtained upstream access or ID tokens and the docs do not claim jti tracking or one-time use for those subject tokens. Reuse of the same upstream JWT MUST be treated as stateless JWT behavior unless the same authorization code is reused; code reuse is the relevant replay check for Dex authorization code flow.

Numeric sentinel analysis: Dex token expiry settings are configured as durations in config (e.g. 10m, 6h). The provided docs do not define 0, -1, or similar sentinel values for disabling or defaulting expiry/authRequest/signingKey settings. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 disables validation or selects a default for these fields without separate source confirmation.

Dex configuration is file-based for connectors, clients, OAuth2 grant settings, and token lifetimes. The provided documentation does not describe REST admin endpoints for enable_auth_method, configure_jwt_validation, create_auth_role, modify_role_config, create_application, or cleanup_auth_method. The fuzzer MUST treat these as out-of-band/static configuration, not runtime HTTP setup calls.

For I2 replay_same_token on oidc_jwt, do NOT flag reuse of the same upstream JWT in Dex token exchange as a vulnerability by default. Dex documentation describes stateless token exchange from upstream OIDC tokens and does not document jti tracking or one-time-use enforcement for submitted subject_token values.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against token_exchange, the sequence MUST include a control exchange using a valid upstream token from the same issuer. Without a control, a failed exchange may be caused by connector misconfiguration (issuer, connector_id, client auth, or missing getUserInfo for access tokens) rather than freshness enforcement.

Token exchange currently works only with the OIDC connector. The fuzzer MUST configure an OIDC connector and use connector_id matching that connector. Testing token exchange against other connector types is invalid for this protocol profile.

When testing token exchange with subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token, the OIDC connector MUST have getUserInfo enabled if the upstream access token is opaque or lacks needed claims. Otherwise Dex may reject or under-populate identity claims for reasons unrelated to the security property under test.

For I1 trust_anchor_substitution and issuer-validation tests in token exchange, the OIDC connector issuer MUST be configured and the submitted subject token is verified against that issuer. A valid test must change the upstream token issuer or connector issuer expectation while keeping other inputs constant.

For I3 config-change sequences involving issuer changes, connector changes, or grant enablement, Dex behavior is driven by static config reload/redeployment rather than documented runtime admin APIs. A valid I3 test must compare behavior before and after a deliberate config change, not assume per-request mutable server state via HTTP.

For I3 authorization-code flow tests, the fuzzer MUST preserve and validate the state parameter across start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token. Dex documentation explicitly relies on state to bind the user who started the flow to the one who finished it and to prevent replay/swap attacks.

For start_oidc_auth, responseTypes controls which flows are enabled. The fuzzer MUST request response_type=code unless the Dex oauth2.responseTypes configuration explicitly enables implicit or hybrid values. Otherwise failures are by configuration, not security enforcement.

For exchange_code_for_token, use application/x-www-form-urlencoded body encoding. Dex documentation shows /token requests as form-encoded for authorization code, password grant, and token exchange. Sending JSON is invalid setup.

For login_with_password, the password grant only works when oauth2.grantTypes includes "password" and oauth2.passwordConnector is set, typically to "local". A failed password-grant request without these settings is expected and must not be interpreted as a security result.

For token_exchange, Dex requires client authentication via Basic Authentication even when the client is marked public for this flow. The fuzzer MUST send client id/secret as HTTP Basic auth and not rely solely on form parameters.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation, requested scope on token exchange MUST be compared against the configured connector/client behavior. Dex examples explicitly allow requesting scopes such as openid groups federated:id during exchange; tests should verify whether exchanged tokens contain claims beyond upstream intent, not assume all additional requested scopes are forbidden by default.

For I5 audience-related tests, Dex supports cross-client trust via the dynamic scope audience:server:client_id:(client-id), but only when the target client explicitly lists the requesting client in trustedPeers. The fuzzer MUST configure trustedPeers for positive cross-client cases; otherwise audience changes should fail by design.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience / ignore_audience style tests, distinguish access_token from id_token semantics carefully. Dex token responses place the bearer credential in access_token, while audience examples in the docs focus heavily on ID token aud/azp claims. The fuzzer MUST inspect the correct token type and claim set for the property being tested.

For I4 multi-identity tests using the OIDC connector, userIDKey controls which upstream claim becomes the Dex user identifier; default is sub. If userIDKey is changed to a mutable or non-unique claim such as nickname, collisions may be by configuration. The fuzzer MUST record which claim is configured as identity source before asserting principal-binding violations.

For I4 and I5 tests involving groups, OIDC connector groups are disabled by default unless insecureEnableGroups is true. If groups scope is requested without enabling group support, missing groups claims are expected and must not be treated as authorization stripping or identity confusion.

For I5 group-based authorization tests on the OIDC connector, allowedGroups is list-membership against exact configured group values. The documentation does not describe wildcard or regex matching for allowedGroups. For multi-identity scenarios requiring different groups to pass the same connector, the fuzzer MUST OMIT allowedGroups rather than set wildcard-like values.

For I4 tests involving group-name transformations, claimModifications may add derived groups, regex-filter groups, or prefix/suffix all group names. The fuzzer MUST disable these modifications unless they are the explicit subject of the test, otherwise apparent identity/authorization mismatches may be by design.

For I4 email-based identity comparisons, overrideClaimMapping=false means standard claims returned in the ID token take precedence over claimMapping. To test alternate-claim identity binding, the fuzzer MUST set overrideClaimMapping=true; otherwise Dex will ignore the mapping when the standard claim is present.

For I1 oidc_request_object_alg_none, Dex certification results indicate unsigned request objects may be either supported correctly or rejected as unsupported, and current status is unknown/interrupted. The fuzzer MUST treat non-200/error rejection as acceptable and only flag a vulnerability if an unsigned request object is accepted and changes security-relevant authorization request parameters.

For I3 PKCE-related tests, Dex certification shows valid PKCE succeeds, but the docs do not state PKCE is universally required. The fuzzer MUST treat missing-PKCE acceptance as a hardening check context and judge by token endpoint status codes, not by identity differences.

For I2 authorization-code replay tests, Dex certification reports code reuse tests as passed/warning, implying code reuse handling exists. The fuzzer MUST test replay by reusing the exact same code at /token and compare HTTP status, not by re-running the whole authorization flow and obtaining a fresh code.

Numeric sentinel analysis: Dex token lifetime settings are documented as durations but no special sentinel values such as 0, -1, or "0s" are documented for disable/default/strict semantics in the provided docs. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 or negative values have special meaning for expiry or rotation settings without external confirmation.

Dex documentation in this corpus exposes dynamic management through gRPC, not documented REST endpoints, for creating clients/connectors/users. Do NOT assume REST admin APIs such as enable_auth_method, configure_jwt_validation, create_application, create_provider, create_user, or cleanup_auth_method exist from these docs.

For I3 state_swap and code_injection tests, start_oidc_auth MUST include a unique state per browser session and the callback exchange MUST use the code returned for that same state. Dex documentation explicitly relies on state to bind the user who started the flow to the one who finished it.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, exchange_code_for_token MUST send the same redirect_uri used at start_oidc_auth. Dex documents standard OAuth2 code flow semantics where the client redeems the returned code with the redirect URI used for the app.

For I3 pkce_skip tests, Dex certification results show valid PKCE succeeds, but the docs do not state PKCE is always required. Treat missing PKCE enforcement as configuration/feature-dependent; assert rejection via non-200 status only when code_challenge/code_verifier are actually part of the test setup.

For I1 oidc_request_object_alg_none tests, send the unsigned request object as the request query parameter to start_oidc_auth. Dex certification notes 'unsigned request object supported correctly or rejected as unsupported' as an open/unknown result, so acceptance is not automatically a vulnerability unless request-object signature requirements were explicitly configured.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against Dex-issued tokens, include a control flow using a freshly obtained valid token from exchange_code_for_token or login_with_password. Without a control, a failed protected-resource call may reflect client setup or unsupported endpoint assumptions rather than token freshness enforcement.

For I2 replay_same_token on upstream JWT token exchange, do NOT flag replay of the same upstream JWT as a vulnerability by default. Dex documentation frames token exchange as stateless verification of an upstream access/ID token and does not document jti tracking or one-time-use semantics for submitted subject_token values.

For I5 token_exchange tests, token_exchange MUST include connector_id naming the OIDC connector that should validate the submitted subject_token. Omitting connector_id makes the request invalid for Dex token exchange and can produce false positives unrelated to audience or scope binding.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, request expanded scope via the scope form field on /token and inspect the returned token claims, not just HTTP 200. Dex supports scopes such as groups and federated:id, and escalation is only meaningful if the exchanged token contains claims beyond the upstream intent.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use the audience form field only when the target client relationship is configured. Dex documents cross-client trust via the dynamic scope audience:server:client_id:(client-id) and trustedPeers; without that setup, audience-related failures are expected and not evidence of correct subject_token audience enforcement.

For I5 cross-client trust tests, remember Dex-issued ID tokens may legitimately contain aud different from the authenticating client and azp equal to the authenticating client when trustedPeers and audience:server:client_id:(client-id) are used. Do not flag this by itself as audience confusion.

offline_access is connector-dependent in Dex. Some connectors, notably SAML and authproxy, do not support refresh tokens, and SAML ignores offline_access. Tests that require refresh_token issuance MUST use a connector documented as supporting refresh tokens or the local/password flow.

Dex refresh tokens are rotated on every refresh by default. If a test reuses an old refresh token after a successful refresh, rejection is BY DESIGN and not an anti-replay bug. The docs also note disableRotation and reuseInterval alter this behavior.

Numeric sentinel analysis: Dex documents no special numeric sentinel values like 0 or -1 for token expiry/rotation in this corpus. Duration settings are configured as explicit duration strings (for example 10m, 6h). Do NOT assume 0 disables or defaults any expiry/rotation behavior unless separately documented in the actual deployment config.
